# songleaf

Dense, readable one-page song sheets: lyrics and chords on one A4 page, with the lyrics as large as will fit.

```bash
pip install songleaf
python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis"    # -> a one-page PDF in ~/.local/share/songleaf/sheets/
```

The default source is the Kaggle *chords-and-lyrics* corpus (about 135,000 songs), read from a local copy of its zip (see [Sources]()).

## What the sheet looks like

- **One page, largest type that fits.** The lyric font size is found by search for each song. On 2,000 randomly sampled corpus songs, the default layout’s median came out around 23 pt, and 1,999 of the 2,000 fit on one page. A song that cannot fit at the minimum size spills onto a second page.
- **Any script the font covers.** Text is set in DejaVu Sans, bundled with the package and embedded in each PDF (Bitstream Vera licence, beside the font files), so Turkish, Greek, Cyrillic and other non-Latin-1 text draws correctly. It is wider than Helvetica, so fitted sizes are somewhat smaller than the numbers above, which were measured in Helvetica; `DenseStyle(lyric_font="Helvetica", ...)` restores the old look.
- **Chords take no line of their own.** They are smaller and blue, start over the syllable they land on, and overlap the tops of the letters of their lyric line.
- **Lines share rows.** Consecutive lines of a paragraph are packed onto one row, separated by a light `/`. A blank line or a new section starts a new row.
- **Small labels.** Sections are grey prefixes (`V1`, `Ch`, `Br`); title, artist, capo and key are one small line at the top.

## Layouts

That is the `dense` layout. Other layouts trade looks for larger lyrics. Name one by joining options with `+`:

| option       | what it changes                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `overlap`    | chords sit lower, on the words themselves, outlined in white and drawn over them: no extra height for chords                                                    |
| `inline`     | chords go in the lyric line, right before the syllable they land on; `‹G` marks a chord that sounds *before* its syllable                                       |
| `packed`     | rows break where the lyrics break (between couplets, not inside a rhyming pair or a repeated line) instead of as late as fits                                   |
| `two-column` | two columns under a full-width heading                                                                                                                          |
| `shaded`     | light bands for choruses and bridges, dark grey for lines already sung, chords coloured by function in the song’s key (tonic darker, outside the key in orange) |
```bash
python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis" --layout inline
python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis" --layout overlap+packed+two-column+shaded
```

The comparison of the largest font size each layout fits, over the same 2,000 songs, is on [songleaf#4](https://github.com/thorwhalen/songleaf/issues/4).

## Command line

```bash
python -m songleaf search "wonderwall oasis"              # one query: list names, then titles, artists, lyrics
python -m songleaf search --artist oasis --lyrics "roads winding"   # narrower: every field given must match
python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis" --output wonderwall.pdf
python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis" --pick 2      # the second-best match
python -m songleaf songs                                  # songs already stored
python -m songleaf export kaggle_chords:1234 --output song.cho   # ChordPro (or --format text); --transpose 2
python -m songleaf viewed                                 # the songs opened, the latest first
python -m songleaf sheet kaggle_chords:1234               # a song by its key: no search
python -m songleaf sheet kaggle_chords:1234 --refresh     # fetch it again from its source
python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis" --transpose 2 # chords up a whole tone, spelled for the new key
python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis" --scale 0.8   # 80% of the size that fills the page
python -m songleaf songbook Campfire                       # a whole list as one PDF: contents, page numbers, bookmarks, in list order
python -m songleaf import chart.txt --title "Paper Boats"   # paste from any site: Ultimate Guitar markup, ChordPro, OpenSong, plain; "-" reads stdin
python -m songleaf sheet paste:ea2a9d845214                 # the key `import` printed
python -m songleaf song kaggle_chords:1234                # the song as data: text, chords, every key's chord table
python -m songleaf build-index                            # once: search from an index, not the whole corpus in memory
```

The `songleaf` console script is the same command.

## Python

```python
import songleaf

hits = songleaf.search("wonderwall oasis")
song = songleaf.get_song(hits[0].key)  # a Song: lyrics text + annotations
songleaf.render_dense_a4(song, "wonderwall.pdf")  # {'font_size': ..., 'pages': 1, ...}
songleaf.render_sheet(song, "wonderwall-inline.pdf", layout="inline+two-column")

songleaf.sheet("wonderwall oasis")  # search, store and render in one call
songleaf.tools.search(
    "wonderwall oasis"
)  # [{..., "match": "title", "highlight": {...}}, ...]
songleaf.sheet("wonderwall oasis", layout="overlap+shaded")
```

A layout is a `SheetLayout(chords=..., packing=..., columns=..., shading=..., style=DenseStyle(...))`. `chords` and `packing` also take your own strategy objects (a `ChordPlacement`, or a packer function with the signature of `songleaf.packing.pack_greedy`):

```python
from functools import partial
from songleaf import SheetLayout, render_sheet
from songleaf.packing import pack_structured

layout = SheetLayout(
    chords="inline", packing=partial(pack_structured, row_cost=5), columns=2
)
render_sheet(song, "sheet.pdf", layout=layout)
```

## The song model

A `Song` is lyrics text plus *standoff* annotations anchored on character offsets, so annotation layers never touch the text:

- `section`: spans its lines, `{"label": "Chorus"}`;
- `chord`: a point on the first character of the syllable the chord lands on, `{"symbol": "G/B", "timing": "at"}` (`"before"` marks a chord that sounds ahead of that syllable);
- `score`: a link from a stretch of lyrics to a score snippet, `{"source", "id", "url", "format"}`.

Metadata (title, artist, capo, key) and provenance (source, id, url, licence) travel with the song, and `Song.to_dict()` is its JSON form.

```python
from songleaf import Song, chord, section, parse_chords_over_lyrics

song = Song(
    "Paper boats drift", [section(0, 17, "Verse 1"), chord(0, "G"), chord(6, "D")]
)
song = parse_chords_over_lyrics(
    "G     D\nPaper boats drift"
)  # the same chords, from a chart
```

## Storage

Songs are kept in a `MutableMapping` (`songleaf.song_store()`): one JSON file per song under `~/.local/share/songleaf/songs/`. Rendered sheets go to `~/.local/share/songleaf/sheets/`. Set `SONGLEAF_DATA_DIR` to move both.

## Sources

`KaggleChordsSource` reads the [chords-and-lyrics dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/eitanbentora/chords-and-lyrics-dataset) through `sung`. It needs a local copy of the zip: put it at `~/.local/share/songleaf/datasets/chords-and-lyrics/chords-and-lyrics-dataset.zip` (under the data root, so `SONGLEAF_DATA_DIR` moves it too), point `SUNG_CHORDS_AND_LYRICS_ZIP` at it, or keep it where `haggle` downloads it (`$HAGGLE_ROOTDIR/zips/eitanbentora/chords-and-lyrics-dataset.zip`). Without a local copy, `sung` downloads it from Kaggle, which needs Kaggle credentials. The corpus was scraped from a chords site, so keep it to personal use.

Loading the corpus takes about five seconds on the first search in a process, and it stays in memory: about 1.1 GB, 1.6 GB once a lyrics search has run. Run `songleaf build-index` once to avoid that. It writes one SQLite file beside the zip (about 190 MB: titles, artists, compressed charts and a full-text index of the words), and from then on the default source reads it. A process then holds about 80 MB for search, a lyrics search takes milliseconds instead of seconds, and the songs and their keys are the same. Run it again after replacing the zip.

Other sources surveyed, plus the Ultimate Guitar / MuseScore decisions, are in [`misc/docs/sources.md`]().

`LocalFolderSource` indexes a folder of files you exported yourself from a paid chords/tab or score site (Ultimate Guitar, MuseScore, …) — text charts are parsed like the Kaggle corpus, score/tab files (Guitar Pro, MusicXML, MSCZ, MIDI, PDF) are attached as a score link. Default folder: `~/.local/share/songleaf/imports/` (moved by `SONGLEAF_DATA_DIR`).

## Web app

`songleaf.web.mk_app()` is a FastAPI app over the same functions: search, `POST /import` (paste a song; the page has a “Paste a song” box), the stored songs, the layout options, and the sheet as JSON, PDF and a PNG per page (for phone browsers that show no PDF inline). It also serves its own page, built phone first: the song starts right under the title and one row of controls. That row holds the text size, the key (−1 / +1, and a key picker that lists every chord of the song beside what it becomes), **Aa** and **⋯**. **Aa** holds the reader’s settings: paper (auto, light, sepia, dark, black), where the chords go (above the words, in the line, or off), one or two columns, shaded choruses, and under *Fine tuning* the colour and opacity of lyrics and chords, chord size, line spacing and font. **⋯** leads to **Print**, which shows the one-page PDF sheet. Its layout starts from the reader’s settings and can be changed there in the same words (chords above, on the words or in the line; rows filled or broken at rhymes; one or two columns; shading). Opacity prints as the matching shade on white paper. The page is a two-line HTML shell that loads its script and style from the app, so it changes with the package.

```bash
pip install "songleaf[web]"
```

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from songleaf.web import mk_app, page_shell

site = FastAPI()
site.mount("/api/songleaf", mk_app())
site.get("/songleaf/", response_class=HTMLResponse)(
    lambda: page_shell(api="/api/songleaf", base="/songleaf")
)
```

**One search field** looks in four places at once and shows what it found in sections, in this order: **In your lists** (lists whose name matches, each opening the library on that list, with its first songs), **Titles**, **Artists** and **Lyrics**. A song appears once, in the first section it fits: a song whose title and lyrics both match is a title match. The matched words are marked, a lyrics match shows the line that matched, and when no title matches a quiet line says so. Titles and artists match word by word: a query can be part of a title (`wonder`), or hold a whole title and artist (`wonderwall oasis`), and a word of four letters or more forgives a typo. In each section the songs whose title and artist hold the most words of the query come first, then the closest, then the most popular. The research and design behind it are on [songleaf#34](https://github.com/thorwhalen/songleaf/pull/34).

**Home** is the library on **Viewed**: the songs you opened, the latest first. It is kept on the server, per person when the host says who is asking (enlace passes the signed-in user; songleaf stores only a hash of the id), so it is the same on every device. The × beside a song takes it out of Viewed, with an Undo; it stays stored and in its lists, and the **Not in a list** chip and search still find it. A house icon at the top of every other view (search results, a list, a song) goes back home; when home is a known number of steps back it walks back to it, so it returns as you left it.

**Lists** work like Gmail labels: a song can be in several lists, and a list can hold other lists. Chips above the songs narrow them to a list (Viewed, each list, Not in a list); choosing a list that holds lists shows them in a second row. The chosen list is in the URL, so Back, reload and a shared link keep it. To file songs, tap the “in …” line under a song’s title (or pick several songs with **Edit** and use **Lists…**): both open the same menu, where you tick lists or create one, then Apply. **Edit** also deletes songs (from storage, every list and Viewed). On a wide screen, **Arrange lists** shows the lists as a tree, where you can drag a song or a list onto a list (that is how lists go inside lists). Lists are shared by everyone using the app (one library). They are kept on the server as a [zodal-groups](https://github.com/i2mint/zodal-groups) snapshot with a revision (`songleaf.library`; the model and its file say “groups”). A save made from an out-of-date revision is refused, and the page replays its changes on top of the newer lists, so two people editing at once don’t overwrite each other.

In Read view, the floating ▶ starts **auto-scroll**; while it runs, − and + set the speed. It is remembered per song, pauses when you touch the song, and keeps the screen awake while running.

The app has no login of its own: put it behind whatever gates the host. It takes the same `sources=` and `store=` as `sheet`. A rendered sheet is kept in memory (`sheet_cache_size=`, default 32), so the page’s requests for one sheet render it once.

## Extending

Three keyword arguments are the extension points, on `sheet` (and `search` for sources):

- `sources=`: objects with a `name`, `search(query, *, title, artist, lyrics, limit)` returning `Hit`s, and `get(song_id)` returning a `Song`;
- `store=`: any `MutableMapping[str, Song]` (a `dict` works);
- `renderer=`: any `(song, output) -> dict` function (`songleaf.make_renderer("inline+shaded", page_size="LETTER")` makes one from a layout). It replaces `layout=`.

```python
songleaf.sheet("paper boats", sources=[my_source], store={}, renderer=my_renderer)
```

# _autosummary/songleaf.chordpro.html.md

# songleaf.chordpro

Parse ChordPro text into a [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song).

ChordPro puts chords inline, in square brackets, at the syllable they land on
(`Paper [G]boats [D]drift`), and describes the song with `{directive: value}`
lines.

- `[X]` becomes a `chord` annotation at that character offset of the
  bracket-free lyric line; a line of chords only becomes an empty text line
  carrying its chords in order, as in [`songleaf.parse`](_autosummary/songleaf.parse.html.md#module-songleaf.parse).
- `{title}`, `{artist}`, `{key}`, `{capo}`, `{tempo}` (and their short
  forms) become metadata.
- `{soc}`/`{eoc}` (and verse, bridge, tab-less variants) and `{c: label}`
  comments become `section` annotations; a section with no lines of its own is
  a *marker* (`{"marker": True}`), as in [`songleaf.parse`](_autosummary/songleaf.parse.html.md#module-songleaf.parse).
- `{x_songleaf_before: 0, 3}` (written by [`songleaf.export.to_chordpro()`](_autosummary/songleaf.export.html.md#songleaf.export.to_chordpro)) marks the
  chords at those positions, counted over the song’s chords in text order, as sounding
  *before* their syllable (`timing="before"`): ChordPro has no way to say it.
- `# comments` and other unknown directives are dropped.

```pycon
>>> song = parse_chordpro("{title: Paper Boats}\n{soc}\nPaper [G]boats [D]drift\n{eoc}")
>>> song.text
'Paper boats drift'
>>> [(a.start, a.body["symbol"]) for a in song.of_kind("chord")]
[(6, 'G'), (12, 'D')]
>>> song.meta["title"], song.of_kind("section")[0].body["label"]
('Paper Boats', 'Chorus')
```

### Module Attributes

| [`BEFORE_DIRECTIVE`](_autosummary/songleaf.chordpro.html.md#songleaf.chordpro.BEFORE_DIRECTIVE)   | The namespaced directive carrying `timing="before"` chords; apps that don't know it skip it.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`parse_chordpro`](_autosummary/songleaf.chordpro.html.md#songleaf.chordpro.parse_chordpro)(raw, \*[, meta, provenance])   | Parse ChordPro text into a `Song`.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|

### songleaf.chordpro.BEFORE_DIRECTIVE *= 'x_songleaf_before'*

The namespaced directive carrying `timing="before"` chords; apps that don’t know it skip it.

### songleaf.chordpro.parse_chordpro(raw, , meta=None, provenance=None)

Parse ChordPro text into a `Song`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **raw** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The ChordPro text.
  * **meta** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Metadata to start from; directives in the text override it.
  * **provenance** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Where the text came from, stored as is.
* **Return type:**

# _autosummary/songleaf.datasets.html.md

# songleaf.datasets

Where the `datasets` data kind lives: local files by default, S3 by configuration.

The corpus files (`chords-and-lyrics/...`) are addressed by their path relative
to the `datasets` kind. ADR-0024 makes the S3 key mirror the local layout, so a
store over disk (`dol.Files`) and a store over S3 (`s3dol`) hold the same
relative keys, and [`dataset_path()`](_autosummary/songleaf.datasets.html.md#songleaf.datasets.dataset_path) is the one place that turns a key into a
real file (SQLite and zip readers need one).

Configuration (environment; `SONGLEAF_DATA_DIR` always wins, so a pinned local
root is never overridden by S3):

- `SONGLEAF_DATASETS_URI`: `s3://bucket/prefix` of the `datasets` kind
  (for example `s3://tw-apps/thorwhalen/songleaf/datasets`). Unset means local.
- `SONGLEAF_S3_PROFILE`: the AWS profile to read with (optional).
- `SONGLEAF_CACHE_DIR`: where S3 objects are cached (default
  `~/.cache/songleaf/datasets`).

### Functions

| [`dataset_path`](_autosummary/songleaf.datasets.html.md#songleaf.datasets.dataset_path)(key, \*[, location])        | The path of a real file for the dataset `key` (relative path), cached if remote.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`datasets_store`](_autosummary/songleaf.datasets.html.md#songleaf.datasets.datasets_store)(\*[, location, readonly]) | The `datasets` kind as a `MutableMapping[str, bytes]` keyed by relative path.      |
| [`s3_location`](_autosummary/songleaf.datasets.html.md#songleaf.datasets.s3_location)([environ])                   | The configured S3 home of the datasets, or `None` when they are local.             |

### Classes

| [`S3Location`](_autosummary/songleaf.datasets.html.md#songleaf.datasets.S3Location)(bucket, prefix[, profile])   |    |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----|

### *class* songleaf.datasets.S3Location(bucket, prefix, profile=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

### songleaf.datasets.dataset_path(key, , location=None)

The path of a real file for the dataset `key` (relative path), cached if remote.

Local: `<data root>/datasets/<key>` (it may not exist). On S3: the object is
downloaded once to the cache (a missing object leaves no file, so the path
does not exist) and the cached path is returned; an object whose size changed
on S3 is fetched again.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### songleaf.datasets.datasets_store(, location=None, readonly=True)

The `datasets` kind as a `MutableMapping[str, bytes]` keyed by relative path.

`dol.Files` over the local folder unless S3 is configured (or `location`
is given), then `s3dol` (the `s3` extra).

The configured S3 home of the datasets, or `None` when they are local.

```pycon

S3Location(bucket='b', prefix='x/datasets/', profile=None)
>>> s3_location({})
```

* **Return type:**
  [`S3Location`](_autosummary/songleaf.datasets.html.md#songleaf.datasets.S3Location) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md

# songleaf.diagrams

Chord diagrams for the sheet: piano keys or guitar shapes (songleaf#13).

The chords a song uses ([`song_chords()`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#songleaf.diagrams.song_chords), in order of first use) are drawn as a strip
of small diagrams. Both kinds come from the chord’s pitch classes alone
([`chord_tones()`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#songleaf.diagrams.chord_tones)), so no fingering table is needed, and none has to be licensed:

- **piano**: a two-octave keyboard with the chord’s notes marked, in close position
  from the bass;
- **guitar**: a shape in standard tuning found by search ([`guitar_shape()`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#songleaf.diagrams.guitar_shape)): the
  lowest sounding string plays the bass (the root, or the slash bass), every chord
  tone sounds, the fret span is at most four frets and four fingers (notes at the
  lowest fret share one barre finger, unless an open string lies under the barre),
  and fewer muted strings, lower positions, fewer fingers and no open string between
  fretted ones are preferred.

The layout reserves the strip’s height before it fits the font size, so the lyrics
shrink to make room ([`strip_height()`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#songleaf.diagrams.strip_height)); [`draw_strip()`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#songleaf.diagrams.draw_strip) draws it.

```pycon
>>> chord_tones("Cmaj7"), chord_tones("Am/G"), chord_tones("F#m7b5")
((0, 4, 7, 11), (7, 9, 0, 4), (6, 9, 0, 4))
>>> guitar_shape("C"), guitar_shape("E"), guitar_shape("G")
((None, 3, 2, 0, 1, 0), (0, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0), (3, 2, 0, 0, 0, 3))
```

| [`STANDARD_TUNING`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#songleaf.diagrams.STANDARD_TUNING)   | Standard guitar tuning, low to high, as pitch classes (E A D G B E).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/songleaf.export.html.md

# songleaf.export

Export a song as ChordPro or as plain text (chords over lyrics), transposition applied.

ChordPro is the fleet’s text interchange: Songbook Pro, OnSong and the ChordPro app read it.
[`to_chordpro()`](_autosummary/songleaf.export.html.md#songleaf.export.to_chordpro) writes what [`songleaf.chordpro.parse_chordpro()`](_autosummary/songleaf.chordpro.html.md#songleaf.chordpro.parse_chordpro) reads, so a song
survives the round trip (text, chords, sections, `title`/`artist`/`key`/`capo`/`tempo`).
A chord that sounds ahead of its syllable (`timing="before"`) has no ChordPro spelling; the
song carries it in the namespaced directive `{x_songleaf_before: ...}`, which other apps ignore.

[`to_text()`](_autosummary/songleaf.export.html.md#songleaf.export.to_text) is the monospaced form: each line of lyrics with its chords on the line above,
a `[Label]` line at each section. It is for reading and pasting; it does not carry timing.

```pycon
>>> from songleaf.model import Song, chord, section
>>> song = Song("Paper boats drift", [chord(6, "G"), chord(12, "D"), section(0, 17, "Chorus")],
...             meta={"title": "Paper Boats"})
>>> print(to_chordpro(song))
{title: Paper Boats}
{start_of_chorus: Chorus}
Paper [G]boats [D]drift
{end_of_chorus}
>>> print(to_text(song))
Paper Boats

[Chorus]
      G     D
Paper boats drift
```

### Module Attributes

| [`FORMATS`](_autosummary/songleaf.export.html.md#songleaf.export.FORMATS)   | name -> (function, file extension, media type).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`to_text`](_autosummary/songleaf.export.html.md#songleaf.export.to_text)(song, \*[, transpose])       | The song as plain text: chords above their syllables, `[Label]` at each section. |

### songleaf.export.FORMATS *= {'chordpro': (<function to_chordpro>, 'cho', 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'), 'text': (<function to_text>, 'txt', 'text/plain; charset=utf-8')}*

# _autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md

# songleaf.harmony

What a chord does in its song’s key, so that sheets can shade chords by function.

The key is estimated from the chords alone (a key given in a chart often names
the sounding key while the chords are written for a capo), and each chord is
then the `"tonic"`, `"diatonic"` (another chord of the key), or `"outside"`
the key (borrowed, secondary dominant, chromatic).

```pycon
>>> key = estimate_key(["G", "D", "Em", "C", "G", "D", "G"])
>>> key
Key(tonic=7, minor=False)
>>> [chord_function(symbol, key) for symbol in ["G", "Em", "C", "Bb", "N.C."]]
['tonic', 'diatonic', 'diatonic', 'outside', None]
>>> estimate_key(["Am", "Dm", "E7", "Am"])
Key(tonic=9, minor=True)
```

### Functions

| [`chord_function`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.chord_function)(symbol, key)                        | `"tonic"`, `"diatonic"` or `"outside"` in `key`; None if `symbol` is not a chord.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`estimate_key`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.estimate_key)(symbols)                              | The key that best explains a song's chords, in order; None if there are no chords.  |
| [`key_name`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.key_name)(key, \*[, flats])                         | `"G"`, `"Bb"`, `"F#m"`: the key spelled as its tonic chord.                         |
| [`parse_chord`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.parse_chord)(symbol)                                | `(root pitch class, quality)`, or None for what is not a chord.                     |
| [`transpose`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.transpose)(song, semitones)                         | A copy of `song` with every chord moved by `semitones`, spelled for the new key.    |
| [`transpose_chord`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.transpose_chord)(symbol, semitones, \*[, flats])    | `symbol` moved by `semitones`: root and bass move, the rest is kept as written.     |
| [`transposition_table`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.transposition_table)(symbols, semitones, \*[, key]) | The chords of a song moved by `semitones`, spelled for the new key.                 |
| [`uses_flats`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.uses_flats)(key)                                    | Whether chords in `key` are spelled with flats (Bb, Eb) rather than sharps.         |

### Classes

| [`Key`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.Key)(tonic[, minor])   | A key: its tonic as a pitch class (C = 0, C# = 1, .   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* songleaf.harmony.Key(tonic, minor=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A key: its tonic as a pitch class (C = 0, C# = 1, … B = 11), major or minor.

### songleaf.harmony.chord_function(symbol, key)

`"tonic"`, `"diatonic"` or `"outside"` in `key`; None if `symbol` is not a chord.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### songleaf.harmony.estimate_key(symbols)

The key that best explains a song’s chords, in order; None if there are no chords.

Each chord scores for a key when it belongs to it, and more when it is its
tonic; a song that starts or ends on a key’s tonic chord scores extra for
that key. Ties go to the major key, and to the lower tonic.

* **Return type:**
  [`Key`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.Key) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### songleaf.harmony.key_name(key, , flats=None)

`"G"`, `"Bb"`, `"F#m"`: the key spelled as its tonic chord.

```pycon
>>> key_name(Key(10)), key_name(Key(6, minor=True)), key_name(Key(6, minor=True), flats=True)
('Bb', 'F#m', 'Gbm')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### songleaf.harmony.parse_chord(symbol)

`(root pitch class, quality)`, or None for what is not a chord.

The quality is `"major"`, `"minor"`, `"diminished"`, or `"open"` (a
suspended or power chord, which has no third). A bass note is ignored. What
the chart parser would not read as a chord (`is_chord_token`) is not one.

```pycon
>>> parse_chord("F#m7"), parse_chord("Bbmaj7/D"), parse_chord("A7sus4"), parse_chord("Bm7b5")
((6, 'minor'), (10, 'major'), (9, 'open'), (11, 'diminished'))
>>> parse_chord("C-7"), parse_chord("Bridge")
((0, 'minor'), None)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### songleaf.harmony.transpose(song, semitones)

A copy of `song` with every chord moved by `semitones`, spelled for the new key.

### songleaf.harmony.transpose_chord(symbol, semitones, , flats=False)

`symbol` moved by `semitones`: root and bass move, the rest is kept as written.

`flats` spells moved notes with flats (choose it from the target key with
[`uses_flats()`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#songleaf.harmony.uses_flats)). What is not a chord comes back unchanged.

```pycon
>>> transpose_chord("G", 2), transpose_chord("F#m7", 1), transpose_chord("C/E", 3, flats=True)
('A', 'Gm7', 'Eb/G')
>>> transpose_chord("Bbmaj7", -1, flats=True), transpose_chord("N.C.", 4), transpose_chord("Am", 0)
('Amaj7', 'N.C.', 'Am')
>>> [transpose_chord(c, 2) for c in ("D7/9", "Bm5-/7", "C6/9", "C(4/9)", "(Em7)", "Am7/G)")]
['E7/9', 'C#m5-/7', 'D6/9', 'D(4/9)', '(F#m7)', 'Bm7/A)']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### songleaf.harmony.transposition_table(symbols, semitones, , key=None)

The chords of a song moved by `semitones`, spelled for the new key.

`symbols` are the song’s chords in order (they give the key when `key` is
not given). Returns `{"semitones", "key", "chords"}`: the new key’s name
(`""` when there are no chords) and `{original: transposed}` over the
distinct chords, in order of first appearance.

```pycon
>>> transposition_table(["G", "D", "Em", "C", "G"], 3)
{'semitones': 3, 'key': 'Bb', 'chords': {'G': 'Bb', 'D': 'F', 'Em': 'Gm', 'C': 'Eb'}}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.harmony.uses_flats(key)

Whether chords in `key` are spelled with flats (Bb, Eb) rather than sharps.

```pycon
>>> uses_flats(Key(5)), uses_flats(Key(7)), uses_flats(Key(2, minor=True)), uses_flats(None)
(True, False, True, False)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)


# _autosummary/songleaf.html.md

# songleaf

songleaf: dense, readable one-page song sheets from searchable sources.

Find a song, keep it as lyrics plus anchored annotations (sections, chords,
provenance, score links), and render it onto one A4 page with the lyrics as
large as will fit.

```pycon
>>> import songleaf
>>> song = songleaf.parse_chords_over_lyrics("C       G\nHello there my friend")
>>> [a.body["symbol"] for a in song.of_kind("chord")]
['C', 'G']
```

From a query to a PDF, on the Kaggle chords-and-lyrics corpus:

```default
songleaf.sheet("wonderwall oasis")   # -> {'path': '.../sheets/oasis-wonderwall.pdf', ...}
```

or `python -m songleaf sheet "wonderwall oasis"`.

### Functions

| [`chord`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.chord)(at, symbol, \*[, timing])                    | A chord landing on the syllable that starts at offset `at`.                                                                |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`fit_font_size`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.fit_font_size)(song, \*[, page_size, margin, ...])  | The largest lyric font size at which `song` fits one page in `layout` (default: v1's).                                     |
| [`get_song`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.get_song)(key, \*[, sources])                       | The song named by `key` (`"<source>:<id>"`), from the source of that name.                                                 |
| [`layout_named`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.layout_named)(spec, \*[, style])                    | The layout of a spec: options of `LAYOUT_OPTIONS` joined by `+` (`"inline+two-column"`).                                   |
| [`layout_spec`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.layout_spec)(spec)                                  | The one spelling of a layout spec, for names: `"Dense"` -> `"dense"`.                                                      |
| [`make_renderer`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.make_renderer)([layout])                            | A `(song, output) -> dict` renderer for `layout`, the shape `sheet`'s `renderer=` takes.                                   |
| [`parse_chords_over_lyrics`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.parse_chords_over_lyrics)(raw, \*[, meta, ...])     | Parse chords-over-lyrics text into a [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.Song).                                |
| [`render_dense_a4`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.render_dense_a4)(song, output, \*[, ...])           | Render `song` in the v1 layout as a PDF to `output` (a path or a binary file object).                                      |
| [`render_sheet`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.render_sheet)(song, output, \*[, layout, ...])      | Render `song` in `layout` (a [`SheetLayout`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.SheetLayout) or a spec) as a PDF to `output`. |
| [`score_link`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.score_link)(start, end, \*, source, id[, url, ...]) | A link from `[start, end)` to a score snippet held by a source.                                                            |
| [`search`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.search)([query, title, artist, lyrics, ...])        | Search every source and merge the hits, best first.                                                                        |
| [`section`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.section)(start, end, label)                         | A section (verse, chorus, ...) spanning `[start, end)`.                                                                    |
| [`sheet`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.sheet)(query, \*[, output, pick, refresh, ...])     | Make a one-page song sheet (PDF) for the best match of `query`.                                                            |
| [`song_store`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.song_store)([rootdir])                              | Songs as JSON files in `rootdir` (default: the `songs` data dir).                                                          |
| [`songs`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.songs)(\*[, store])                                 | The keys of the stored songs.                                                                                              |

### Classes

### *class* songleaf.KaggleChordsSource(, loader=None, min_score=70)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The Kaggle *chords-and-lyrics* corpus (~135K songs, chords over lyrics).

Read through `sung` from a local copy of the zip, with no Kaggle
credentials needed when that copy exists. The corpus was scraped from a
chords site: personal use only (licence tag `gray`).

Title and artist are matched fuzzily (typos, punctuation and word order
do not matter); lyrics must contain every word of the `lyrics` query as a
whole word. Lyrics matches are not ranked beyond popularity.

* **Parameters:**
  * **loader** – `() -> pandas.DataFrame` with `columns`. Defaults to
    sung’s loader of the local corpus zip.
  * **min_score** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Fuzzy-match cutoff, 0-100.

#### get(song_id)

The song with this id, parsed into a [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.Song).

* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)

#### search(query='', , title='', artist='', lyrics='', limit=10)

Songs matching every given constraint, best first.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Hit`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.Hit)]

#### search_tiers(query, , limit=10)

The songs whose title, artist or lyrics match `query`, by where they match.

`{"title": [...], "artist": [...], "lyrics": [...]}`, at most `limit` in each,
best first. A song is in the first kind it matches, even when it ranks below the
limit there, so a song is never shown as an artist match because more titles
matched.

Title and artist match word by word ([`WordIndex`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.WordIndex)): the query
is inside the field (`"wonder"` finds *Wonderwall*) or the field is inside the
query (`"wonderwall oasis"` finds the title *Wonderwall* and the artist *Oasis*),
a word of four letters or more forgiving a typo; or every word of the query is in
the title or in the artist (`"paper boats invented band"`). A song whose title
holds a word of the query that its artist does not is a title match
(`"wonderwall oasis"`: *Wonderwall (ver. 2)* by Oasis), otherwise an artist match. Within each kind, the songs whose
title and artist together hold the most words of the query come first (so
*Wonderwall* by Oasis leads), then the closest by fuzzy score (of the title, or of
title and artist, whichever is closer; of the artist), then the most popular.
Lyrics hold every word of the query, rank by popularity, and carry
`meta["snippet"]`: the line that matched, with its spans.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Hit`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.Hit)]]

### *class* songleaf.SheetLayout(chords='over', packing='greedy', columns=1, shading=False, diagrams=None, style=DenseStyle(), score=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

    `"inline"` (in the line, before their syllable), or any

  * **packing** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)) – Which lines share a row: `"greedy"` or `"structured"`, or
    any packer with the signature of [`songleaf.packing.pack_greedy()`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.pack_greedy).
  * **columns** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Columns per page.

    of diagrams at the foot of the first page ([`songleaf.diagrams`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#module-songleaf.diagrams));
    the lyrics shrink to make room. `None`: no diagrams.
  * **score** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Draw the song’s score snippet, if its provider has one, above

* **Parameters:**

  * **annotations** ([`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Annotation`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Annotation)]) – Standoff annotations over `text` (kept sorted by start).
  * **meta** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – Descriptive fields: `title`, `artist`, `capo`, `key`, …
  * **provenance** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – Where the song came from: `source`, `id`, `url`, `license`.

The same as [`render_sheet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.render_sheet) with `layout="dense"`. Returns

### songleaf.render_sheet(song, output, , layout='dense', page_size='A4', margin=14.0, min_font_size=6.0, max_font_size=72.0, scale=1.0, snippets=None)

Render `song` in `layout` (a [`SheetLayout`](_autosummary/songleaf.html.md#songleaf.SheetLayout) or a spec) as a PDF to `output`.

The lyric font size is the largest that fits the song on one page, times
`scale`: `1` fills the page, `0.8` leaves room, `1.2` is larger type
that runs onto a second page. It never goes past `max_font_size`.

`snippets` provides a `score` layout’s snippet: `song -> ScoreSnippet | None`
(default [`songleaf.snippets.abc_snippet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md#songleaf.snippets.abc_snippet)).

`output` is a path or a binary file object. Returns
`{"path", "font_size", "pages", "rows"}`; `path` is `None` when
`output` is a file object.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.score_link(start, end, , source, id, url='', format='', notation='', rule='')

A link from `[start, end)` to a score snippet held by a source.

`notation` holds a short snippet inline (`format` says in what, such as
`"abc"`); `rule` names the rule that chose the stretch (`"chosen"`
when picked by hand). Both are left out of the body when empty.

* **Return type:**
  [`Annotation`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Annotation)

### songleaf.search(query='', , title='', artist='', lyrics='', limit=10, sources=None)

Search every source and merge the hits, best first.

```pycon
>>> search("paper boats", sources=[])
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Hit`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.Hit)]

### songleaf.section(start, end, label)

A section (verse, chorus, …) spanning `[start, end)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Annotation`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Annotation)

### songleaf.sheet(query, , output='', pick=1, refresh=False, layout='dense', transpose=0, scale=1.0, sources=None, store=None, renderer=None)

Make a one-page song sheet (PDF) for the best match of `query`.

`query` may also be a song key, as `search` and `songs` show them
(`kaggle_chords:1234`): a stored song renders without searching, and the
key of a known source is fetched from it directly. `pick` chooses the n-th
best match instead of the best. The song is saved to the store; `refresh`
fetches it from its source again, replacing the stored copy. The PDF goes to
`output`, by default the `sheets` data directory.

`layout` is `dense` (the default), or options joined with `+`:
`overlap` (chords over the words themselves), `inline` (chords in the
line, before their syllable), `packed` (rows break where the lyrics do),
`two-column`, `shaded` (sections, repeated lines and chord functions);
for example `inline+packed+two-column`. A `renderer` decides the layout
itself, so it does not go with `layout` or `scale`.

`transpose` moves every chord by that many semitones (spelled for the new
key); the stored song keeps its chords. `scale` multiplies the font size
that fills the page: `0.8` for smaller type, `1.2` for larger type over
more pages.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.song_store(rootdir=None)

Songs as JSON files in `rootdir` (default: the `songs` data dir).

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)]

### songleaf.songs(, store=None)

The keys of the stored songs.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

# _autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md

# songleaf.importers

Turn pasted text into a [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song): a registry of format importers.

Each [`Importer`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.Importer) is a strategy: `detect(text)` says whether the text is
in its format, `parse(text, meta=, provenance=)` builds the song. The registry
[`IMPORTERS`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.IMPORTERS) is tried in order and the first match wins; the last one
(plain chords-over-lyrics) matches anything, so `import_text()` always
answers. A new format is a new [`Importer`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.Importer) in the registry, or one passed
as `importers=`.

- `ultimate-guitar`: `[ch]G[/ch]` / `[tab]...[/tab]` markup, stripped to
  columns, then parsed as chords-over-lyrics (`[Verse 1]` headers become
  sections).
- `chordpro`: `{directive}` lines or `[G]` chords inline in the lyrics.
- `opensong`: lines prefixed `.` (chords), \`\` \`\` (lyrics), `;` (comment),
  `[V1]`-style section tags.
- `chords-over-lyrics`: the fallback.

songleaf never contacts the site the text came from.

```pycon
>>> import_song("[ch]G[/ch]    [ch]D[/ch]\nPaper boats drift").format
'ultimate-guitar'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`PASTE_PROVENANCE`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.PASTE_PROVENANCE)   | Provenance recorded for every pasted song (`url` is added when known).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`KEY_HASH_CHARS`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.KEY_HASH_CHARS)     | Characters of the text hashed into the `paste:<hash>` key.               |
| [`MAX_META_CHARS`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.MAX_META_CHARS)     | Characters a given `key` or `capo` may have at most (`"F#m"`, `"2"`).    |
| [`MAX_PASTE_CHARS`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.MAX_PASTE_CHARS)    | Pasted text longer than this is refused (a chord chart is a few KB).     |
| [`IMPORTERS`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.IMPORTERS)          | Tried in order; the last one accepts anything.                           |

### Functions

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `format_names`([importers])                                                                       |                                                                               |
| [`import_song`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.import_song)(text, \*[, title, artist, url, ...]) | Parse pasted *text* with the first importer that recognises it (or *format*). |
| [`paste_key`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.paste_key)(text)                                  | The store key of pasted *text*: `paste:<hash>` (the same text, the same key). |

### Classes

|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

The name of the first importer that recognises *text*.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### songleaf.importers.import_song(text, \*, title='', artist='', url='', key='', capo='', format='', importers=(Importer(name='ultimate-guitar', detect=<function <lambda>>, parse=<function \_parse_ultimate_guitar>), Importer(name='chordpro', detect=<function \_is_chordpro>, parse=<function parse_chordpro>), Importer(name='opensong', detect=<function <lambda>>, parse=<function \_parse_opensong>), Importer(name='chords-over-lyrics', detect=<function <lambda>>, parse=<function parse_chords_over_lyrics>)))

`title`/`artist`/`key`/`capo` given here win over those in the text.
A `url` on ultimate-guitar.com is checked first (official and Pro pages are
refused, see [`songleaf.ultimate_guitar`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#module-songleaf.ultimate_guitar)), keys the song `ug:<id>`
instead of `paste:<hash>`, and is noted as `provenance.site`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Imported`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.Imported)

# _autosummary/songleaf.kaggle_index.html.md

# songleaf.kaggle_index

A search index of the Kaggle corpus: the same songs and keys, without the corpus in memory.

[`KaggleChordsSource`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.KaggleChordsSource) holds the whole corpus as a
DataFrame: about 1.1 GB per process, 1.6 GB once a lyrics search has run, and
every web worker holds its own copy. [`build_kaggle_index()`](_autosummary/songleaf.kaggle_index.html.md#songleaf.kaggle_index.build_kaggle_index) writes it once
to one SQLite file beside the zip (`datasets/chords-and-lyrics/`): titles,
artists, popularity, each chart zlib-compressed, and an FTS5 table of the
charts’ words. [`KaggleChordsIndex`](_autosummary/songleaf.kaggle_index.html.md#songleaf.kaggle_index.KaggleChordsIndex) reads that file. It keeps only the
titles, artists and popularity in memory (for fuzzy matching, a few tens of MB)
and answers lyrics searches and song lookups from disk.

Search results are the DataFrame source’s: the ranking code is shared, and only
where the data comes from differs. The one difference is how lyrics split into
words: FTS5’s tokenizer treats `_` as a separator and does not compose
decomposed accents, where the DataFrame source’s regular expression does the
opposite. Rebuilding the index while a server runs is safe: a process that
notices the file changed reloads it.

```pycon
>>> import pandas as pd, tempfile, os
>>> corpus = pd.DataFrame({
...     "Unnamed: 0": [1, 2], "artist_name": ["The Band", "Other"],
...     "song_name": ["Paper Boats", "Quiet Road"], "lang": ["en", "en"],
...     "popularity": [3, 1], "chords&lyrics": ["G\nPaper boats drift", "C\nquiet road"],
... })
>>> path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "index.sqlite")
>>> build_kaggle_index(path=path, loader=lambda: corpus)["songs"]
2
>>> [hit.key for hit in KaggleChordsIndex(path).search(lyrics="boats")]
['kaggle_chords:1']
```

| [`KAGGLE_INDEX_NAME`](_autosummary/songleaf.kaggle_index.html.md#songleaf.kaggle_index.KAGGLE_INDEX_NAME)   | The index's file name, beside the corpus zip under `datasets/`.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`kaggle_index_path`](_autosummary/songleaf.kaggle_index.html.md#songleaf.kaggle_index.kaggle_index_path)()                                  | Where the index is read from: beside the corpus zip under the data root.        |

### *class* songleaf.kaggle_index.KaggleChordsIndex(path=None, , min_score=70)

Bases: [`KaggleChordsSource`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.KaggleChordsSource)

The Kaggle corpus read from its index ([`build_kaggle_index()`](_autosummary/songleaf.kaggle_index.html.md#songleaf.kaggle_index.build_kaggle_index)).

The same `name` and ids as `KaggleChordsSource`, so song keys and
stored songs carry over. Only the columns fuzzy matching needs are held in
memory; charts and lyrics matches come from the file.

#### get(song_id)

The song with this id, parsed into a `Song`.

#### search(query='', \*\*constraints)

Songs matching every given constraint, best first.

#### search_tiers(query, , limit=10)

The songs whose title, artist or lyrics match `query`, by where they match.

`{"title": [...], "artist": [...], "lyrics": [...]}`, at most `limit` in each,
best first. A song is in the first kind it matches, even when it ranks below the
limit there, so a song is never shown as an artist match because more titles
matched.

Title and artist match word by word ([`WordIndex`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.WordIndex)): the query
is inside the field (`"wonder"` finds *Wonderwall*) or the field is inside the
query (`"wonderwall oasis"` finds the title *Wonderwall* and the artist *Oasis*),
a word of four letters or more forgiving a typo; or every word of the query is in
the title or in the artist (`"paper boats invented band"`). A song whose title
holds a word of the query that its artist does not is a title match
(`"wonderwall oasis"`: *Wonderwall (ver. 2)* by Oasis), otherwise an artist match. Within each kind, the songs whose
title and artist together hold the most words of the query come first (so
*Wonderwall* by Oasis leads), then the closest by fuzzy score (of the title, or of
title and artist, whichever is closer; of the artist), then the most popular.
Lyrics hold every word of the query, rank by popularity, and carry
`meta["snippet"]`: the line that matched, with its spans.

### songleaf.kaggle_index.build_kaggle_index(, path=None, loader=None, batch_size=5000)

Write the index of the Kaggle corpus (`loader`: as for `KaggleChordsSource`).

Loading the corpus takes the memory the index exists to avoid, so run this
once, apart from any server (`songleaf build-index`). The file is written
beside the target and moved into place when complete, so a reader never
sees half an index.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.kaggle_index.kaggle_index_path()

Where the index is read from: beside the corpus zip under the data root.

When the datasets live on S3 (`songleaf.datasets`), this is the cached
download of the index (fetched on first use), a real file for SQLite.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md

# songleaf.library

The library’s lists: which stored songs are in which lists, shared by everyone using it.

The page calls them *lists*; the model and the stored file keep the name zodal-groups gives
them (groups), so this module and `groups.json` say “groups”.

The groups are a zodal-groups snapshot (`{"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]}`: songs and
groups are nodes, a membership is an edge from a group to a song or to another group). The
page edits them with zodal-groups and saves the whole snapshot; this module keeps it as one
JSON document under the data root (`library/groups.json`) with a revision number.

A save names the revision it was made from. If the document has moved on since (someone
else saved), the save is refused with [`RevisionConflict`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.RevisionConflict), which carries the current
document, so no one’s change is silently overwritten.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> read_groups(root=root)
{'revision': 0, 'snapshot': {'nodes': [], 'edges': []}}
>>> snapshot = {"nodes": [{"id": "Family"}, {"id": "memory:1"}],
...             "edges": [{"id": "e1", "parent": "Family", "child": "memory:1",
...                        "kind": "contains"}]}
>>> save_groups(snapshot, revision=0, root=root)["revision"]
1
>>> drop_item("memory:1", root=root)["snapshot"]["edges"]
[]
```

### Module Attributes

| [`MAX_BYTES`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.MAX_BYTES)   | thousands of songs fit many times over.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`checked_snapshot`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.checked_snapshot)(snapshot)                       | `snapshot` if it has the shape of a zodal-groups snapshot, else `ValueError`.                    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`drop_item`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.drop_item)(item, \*[, root])                      | Take `item` (a song key) out of every group; returns the document, saved if it changed.          |
| [`file_lock`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.file_lock)(path)                                  | One writer of `path` at a time: threads of this process, and other processes where fcntl exists. |
| [`list_members`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.list_members)(snapshot, list_id)                  | The songs in a list or in any list inside it, each once, in the order they were added.           |
| [`list_names`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.list_names)(snapshot)                             | `{id: name}` of every list (group) in a snapshot: its nodes, and every edge's parent.            |
| [`lists_matching`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.lists_matching)(query, snapshot)                  | The lists whose name the query names, best first: `[{"id", "name", "spans"}]`.                   |
| [`read_groups`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.read_groups)(\*[, root])                          | `{"revision", "snapshot"}`: the current groups, revision 0 when there are none.                  |
| [`save_groups`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.save_groups)(snapshot, \*, revision[, root, ...]) | Replace the groups with `snapshot`, made from `revision`; returns the new document.              |
| [`write_json_atomically`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.write_json_atomically)(path, document)            | Write `document` to `path` so that readers see the old file or the new one, never half.          |

### Exceptions

| [`RevisionConflict`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.RevisionConflict)(current)   | The groups changed since the revision a save was made from.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|

### songleaf.library.MAX_BYTES *= 2000000*

thousands of songs fit many times over.

* **Type:**
  The largest groups document accepted, in bytes

### *exception* songleaf.library.RevisionConflict(current)

Bases: [`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#Exception)

The groups changed since the revision a save was made from.

### songleaf.library.checked_snapshot(snapshot)

`snapshot` if it has the shape of a zodal-groups snapshot, else `ValueError`.

The checks are zodal-groups’ own read-path rules (`parseSnapshot`: non-empty string
ids, unique node and edge ids, every edge with a parent, a child and a kind), plus no
self-loop and no cycle, so a page can always load what was saved. The profile’s other
rules are zodal-groups’, applied where the edit is made.

```pycon
>>> edge = {"id": "e", "parent": "a", "child": "a", "kind": "contains"}
>>> checked_snapshot({"nodes": [], "edges": [edge]})
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: edges[0]: a group cannot contain itself ('a')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.library.drop_item(item, , root=None)

Take `item` (a song key) out of every group; returns the document, saved if it changed.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.library.file_lock(path)

One writer of `path` at a time: threads of this process, and other processes where fcntl exists.

### songleaf.library.list_members(snapshot, list_id)

The songs in a list or in any list inside it, each once, in the order they were added.

```pycon
>>> snap = {"nodes": [], "edges": [
...     {"id": "1", "parent": "Campfire", "child": "x:1", "kind": "contains"},
...     {"id": "2", "parent": "Campfire", "child": "Slow", "kind": "contains"},
...     {"id": "3", "parent": "Slow", "child": "x:2", "kind": "contains"},
...     {"id": "4", "parent": "Slow", "child": "x:1", "kind": "contains"}]}
>>> list_members(snap, "Campfire")
['x:1', 'x:2']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### songleaf.library.list_names(snapshot)

`{id: name}` of every list (group) in a snapshot: its nodes, and every edge’s parent.

```pycon
>>> list_names({"nodes": [{"id": "a", "label": "Campfire"}],
...             "edges": [{"id": "e", "parent": "b", "child": "x:1", "kind": "contains"}]})
{'a': 'Campfire', 'b': 'b'}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### songleaf.library.lists_matching(query, snapshot)

The lists whose name the query names, best first: `[{"id", "name", "spans"}]`.

A list matches when every word of the query starts a word of its name (`"camp"`
finds Campfire, `"to le"` finds To learn; a one-letter word must be a whole word), or
when the whole name, four letters or more, is the query give or take one typo (a
letter added, dropped, changed or two swapped). So a short name (`Fun`) is not found
by every query that holds it (`funeral`, `funk`). `spans` are the matched parts
of the name.

```pycon
>>> snap = {"nodes": [{"id": "Campfire"}, {"id": "To learn"}, {"id": "Fun"}], "edges": []}
>>> [m["id"] for m in lists_matching("camp", snap)]
['Campfire']
>>> [m["id"] for m in lists_matching("campfier", snap)], lists_matching("funk", snap)
(['Campfire'], [])
>>> lists_matching("t", snap)
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### songleaf.library.read_groups(, root=None)

`{"revision", "snapshot"}`: the current groups, revision 0 when there are none.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.library.save_groups(snapshot, , revision, root=None, keep_item=None)

Replace the groups with `snapshot`, made from `revision`; returns the new document.

`keep_item(id) -> bool`, when given, decides whether a member that is not a group (an
item: a song key) may stay; memberships of the others are dropped (a song deleted while
a page that still showed it was saving). Raises [`RevisionConflict`](_autosummary/songleaf.library.html.md#songleaf.library.RevisionConflict) when the
stored revision is not `revision`, and `ValueError` when `snapshot` is not a
snapshot or `revision` not a whole number.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.library.write_json_atomically(path, document)

Write `document` to `path` so that readers see the old file or the new one, never half.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md

# songleaf.match

Where a query matched: the words it shares with a field, as spans to highlight, and the lyric line.

Pure text functions, no corpus and no I/O. The search tags each hit with the field it
matched ([`MATCH_KINDS`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.MATCH_KINDS)); these say *where* in that field, so the page can mark the
matched part without tokenizing anything itself.

Words are runs of letters and digits, compared case-insensitively; a query word marks a
word of the text that it starts (`"wond"` marks `"Wonderwall"`), so a partly typed
word is shown too. A fuzzy match with a typo marks nothing, which is honest: the words
are not there.

```pycon
>>> word_spans("Paper Boats", "paper")
[[0, 5]]
>>> lyric_snippet("G       D\nPaper boats drift down\nC\nthe silver stream", "silver stream")
{'text': 'the silver stream', 'spans': [[4, 10], [11, 17]]}
```

### Module Attributes

| [`MATCH_KINDS`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.MATCH_KINDS)       | a song in a list whose name matches, then title, artist and lyrics.                                                                                                     |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TYPO_MIN_LENGTH`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.TYPO_MIN_LENGTH)   | A query word this long or longer also finds the words one edit away (a letter added, dropped, changed, or two swapped); from `TWO_TYPOS_MIN_LENGTH` letters, two edits. |
| [`PREFIX_MIN_LENGTH`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.PREFIX_MIN_LENGTH) | A query word shorter than this finds only itself, not every word it starts ("a").                                                                                       |
| [`MAX_QUERY_WORDS`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.MAX_QUERY_WORDS)   | a pasted verse stops here.                                                                                                                                              |

### Functions

| [`lyric_snippet`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.lyric_snippet)(text, query, \*[, width])   | The line of `text` holding the most words of `query` (whole words), with their spans.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`query_words`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.query_words)(query)                        | The distinct words of a query, lowercased, in order; `10,000` is the word `10000`.      |
| [`shared_words`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.shared_words)(query, text)                 | How many distinct words of `query` are words of `text`.                                 |
| [`word_spans`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.word_spans)(text, query)                   | `[start, end]` of each word of `text` that a word of `query` starts, in order.          |

### Classes

| [`WordIndex`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.WordIndex)(texts)   | Which of a list of texts (titles, say) hold which words, for matching a query word by word.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### songleaf.match.MATCH_KINDS *= ('list', 'title', 'artist', 'lyrics')*

a song in a list
whose name matches, then title, artist and lyrics. A song is reported once, in its first kind.

* **Type:**
  The kinds of match a search reports, in the order the page shows them

### songleaf.match.MAX_QUERY_WORDS *= 12*

a pasted verse stops here.

* **Type:**
  The words of a query that are matched against titles and artists

### songleaf.match.PREFIX_MIN_LENGTH *= 2*

A query word shorter than this finds only itself, not every word it starts (“a”).

### songleaf.match.TYPO_MIN_LENGTH *= 4*

A query word this long or longer also finds the words one edit away (a letter added,
dropped, changed, or two swapped); from `TWO_TYPOS_MIN_LENGTH` letters, two edits.

### *class* songleaf.match.WordIndex(texts)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Which of a list of texts (titles, say) hold which words, for matching a query word by word.

A text matches a query when the query is *inside* it (every query word is a word of the
text, or starts one: `"paper bo"` finds *Paper Boats*) or the text is inside the query
(every word of the text is a word of the query, two at least: `"paper boats band"`
finds *Paper Boats*). In the first direction, a query word of [`TYPO_MIN_LENGTH`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.TYPO_MIN_LENGTH) letters or more
also matches the words it is a typo of; in the second, the text’s words must be there as
typed, or every short title would be a typo of some word of a long query. Unlike a fuzzy score over the whole string, a word is never matched by
a piece of another word, so *As* is not a match for `"oasis"`.

Memory: one sorted vocabulary, one array of row numbers per text word, and one word
count per text, a few MB for 135K titles.

```pycon
>>> titles = WordIndex(["Paper Boats", "Quiet Road", "Paper Moon", "As"])
>>> sorted(titles.matching("paper"))
[0, 2]
>>> sorted(titles.matching("paper boats by the band")), sorted(titles.matching("papr boats"))
([0], [0])
>>> sorted(WordIndex(["Scream"]).matching("silver stream"))  # one letter from "stream"
[]
>>> sorted(WordIndex(["Day", "The Day"]).matching("is gonna be the day"))  # one word is not enough
[1]
>>> sorted(titles.matching("oasis")), sorted(titles.matching("qui"))
([], [1])
```

#### matching(query)

The rows whose text holds the query, or is held by it, word by word.

* **Return type:**
  [`set`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#set)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

#### rows_with(word)

The rows holding `word` (a query word, lowercased), a word it starts, or one it is a typo of.

```pycon
>>> sorted(WordIndex(["Paper Boats", "Paperback", "Quiet"]).rows_with("paper"))
[0, 1]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`set`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#set)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### songleaf.match.lyric_snippet(text, query, , width=90)

The line of `text` holding the most words of `query` (whole words), with their spans.

Lyrics match on whole words (as the search does), so a span here is a whole word.
A line longer than `width` is cut around its first match, with `…` marking each
cut. `None` when no line holds any of the words.

```pycon
>>> lyric_snippet("la la\nno match here", "boats") is None
True
>>> long = "word " * 30 + "boats " + "word " * 30
>>> cut = lyric_snippet(long, "boats", width=30)
>>> cut["text"].startswith("…") and cut["text"].endswith("…"), len(cut["text"]) <= 32
(True, True)
>>> cut["text"][slice(*cut["spans"][0])]
'boats'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### songleaf.match.query_words(query)

The distinct words of a query, lowercased, in order; `10,000` is the word `10000`.

```pycon
>>> query_words("Paper  boats, PAPER!"), query_words("10,000 Hours")
(['paper', 'boats'], ['10000', 'hours'])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### songleaf.match.shared_words(query, text)

How many distinct words of `query` are words of `text`.

```pycon
>>> shared_words("10000 hours justin bieber", "10,000 Hours Justin Bieber")
4
```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### songleaf.match.word_spans(text, query)

`[start, end]` of each word of `text` that a word of `query` starts, in order.

```pycon
>>> word_spans("Wonderwall (Remastered)", "wonder rem")
[[0, 10], [12, 22]]
>>> word_spans("Quiet Road", "road quiet")
[[0, 5], [6, 10]]
>>> word_spans("Quiet Road", "")
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]


# _autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md

# songleaf.model

The linked-artifact model: a song is lyrics text plus standoff annotations.

A [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song) keeps its lyrics as one plain string and everything else as
[`Annotation`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Annotation) records anchored on character offsets into that string.
The text is never marked up, so any number of annotation layers can coexist
and be added later without touching the lyrics (the standoff design of
`lacing`, over characters instead of seconds).

Kinds used so far:

- `"section"`: spans the section’s lines, `body={"label": "Chorus"}`. A
  label-only section (a bare `[Chorus]` marker meaning “repeat the chorus”) is
  empty (`start == end`), sits on an empty line of its own, and has
  `"marker": True` in its body.
- `"chord"`: a point (`start == end`) on the first character of the
  syllable the chord lands on, `body={"symbol": "G/B", "timing": "at"}`.
  `timing` is `"at"` (the chord sounds with that syllable, the default) or
  `"before"` (it sounds ahead of it). Chords of a line with no lyrics (an
  intro, an instrumental bar) sit, in order, on an empty line of the text.
- `"score"`: a link to a score snippet for `[start, end)`,
  `body={"source": ..., "id": ..., "url": ..., "format": ...}`.
- `"time"`: a point at the start of a lyric line, when the recording reaches it,
  `body={"ms": 61230, "source": "lrc"}` ([`songleaf.timing`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#module-songleaf.timing)). Only times, never
  the text they were aligned from.

`meta["media"]` holds the recording’s ids: `{"youtube": ..., "spotify": ...}`.

```pycon
>>> song = Song("Hello there", [chord(0, "C"), chord(6, "G")], meta={"title": "Hi"})
>>> [(a.start, a.body["symbol"]) for a in song.of_kind("chord")]
[(0, 'C'), (6, 'G')]
>>> Song.from_dict(song.to_dict()) == song
True
```

### Module Attributes

| [`CHORD_TIMINGS`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.CHORD_TIMINGS)   | When a chord sounds, relative to the syllable it is anchored on.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`score_link`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.score_link)(start, end, \*, source, id[, url, ...]) | A link from `[start, end)` to a score snippet held by a source. |
