A link from `[start, end)` to a score snippet held by a source.

`notation` holds a short snippet inline (`format` says in what, such as
`"abc"`); `rule` names the rule that chose the stretch (`"chosen"`
when picked by hand). Both are left out of the body when empty.

* **Return type:**
  [`Annotation`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Annotation)

### songleaf.model.section(start, end, label)

A section (verse, chorus, …) spanning `[start, end)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Annotation`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Annotation)


# _autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md

# songleaf.packing

Line packing: which consecutive lines of a paragraph share a row.

A *packer* takes the widths of consecutive units (lines, or the parts of a
wrapped line), the row `width` and the `separator` width, and returns the
rows as `(start, stop)` index ranges, in order. It never reorders units, and a
unit wider than the row gets a row of its own.

- [`pack_greedy()`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.pack_greedy) puts as many units on each row as fit (the v1 packing).
- [`pack_structured()`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.pack_structured) finds the packing of least total cost: every row costs
  `row_cost`, and every break between rows costs what breaking the lyric there
  costs (`break_costs`, usually from [`line_break_costs()`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.line_break_costs)): nothing
  between quatrains, little between couplets, a lot inside a rhyming pair or
  between a line and its repeat.

A five-line verse where three lines fit on a row: greedy packing leaves a
couplet split across rows, structured packing does not, on as many rows.

```pycon
>>> verse = ["one", "two", "three", "four", "five"]
>>> pack_greedy([2] * 5, width=6.5, separator=0.25)
[(0, 3), (3, 5)]
>>> pack_structured([2] * 5, width=6.5, separator=0.25, break_costs=line_break_costs(verse))
[(0, 2), (2, 5)]
>>> rhyme_key("Paper boats on a silver stream"), rhyme_key("a morning dream")
('eam', 'eam')
```

### Functions

| [`line_break_costs`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.line_break_costs)(lines, \*[, ...])               | The cost of a row break after each line of a paragraph but the last.                          |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`pack_greedy`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.pack_greedy)(widths, \*, width, separator[, ...]) | As many units on each row as fit.                                                             |
| [`pack_structured`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.pack_structured)(widths, \*, width, separator)    | The rows of least `row_cost * rows + sum(break_costs at the breaks)`.                         |
| [`rhyme_key`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.rhyme_key)(line)                                  | The sound a line ends on, as letters: the last vowel group of its last word and what follows. |

### songleaf.packing.line_break_costs(lines, , between_quatrains=0.0, between_couplets=0.3, inside_couplet=1.0, rhyme=1.0, repeat=0.5)

The cost of a row break after each line of a paragraph but the last.

Counting from the paragraph’s first line, a break after every fourth line
costs `between_quatrains`, after every other even line
`between_couplets`, and after an odd line `inside_couplet`. A break
right before or after a rhyming pair costs no more than
`between_couplets` (so a pickup line shifts the couplets), a break
between two lines that rhyme costs `rhyme` more, and one between a line
and its repeat `repeat` more.

```pycon
>>> line_break_costs(["a stream", "a dream", "go slow", "go low"])
[2.0, 0.3, 2.0]
>>> line_break_costs(["well", "a stream", "a dream", "go slow", "go slow"])
[0.3, 1.3, 0.3, 1.5]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### songleaf.packing.pack_greedy(widths, , width, separator, break_costs=())

As many units on each row as fit. `break_costs` is accepted and ignored.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

### songleaf.packing.pack_structured(widths, , width, separator, break_costs=(), row_cost=2.0)

The rows of least `row_cost * rows + sum(break_costs at the breaks)`.

`break_costs[k]` is the cost of a break between unit `k` and `k + 1`
(missing entries cost nothing). With every break free this uses as few rows
as [`pack_greedy()`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#songleaf.packing.pack_greedy), and ties go to the greedy packing.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

### songleaf.packing.rhyme_key(line)

The sound a line ends on, as letters: the last vowel group of its last word and what follows.

A silent final `e` is dropped first, so `love` and `above` share
`"ov"`. Accents are ignored, and a trailing note such as `(x2)` is skipped.

```pycon
>>> rhyme_key("sing it low (x2)"), rhyme_key("Coração"), rhyme_key("")
('ow', 'ao', '')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/songleaf.parse.html.md

# songleaf.parse

Parse chords-over-lyrics text into a [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song).

This is the format most chord sites use, and the one in the Kaggle corpus: a
line of chord symbols, column-aligned over the lyric line it belongs to.

- Each chord is anchored on the syllable under it (a chord over a space moves
  to the start of the next syllable).
- A chord line with no lyric line under it (an intro, a solo) becomes an empty
  text line carrying its chords in order.
- Section headers (`Verse 1:`, `[Chorus]`, `Intro 2x: G D`) become
  section annotations; a header with no lines of its own is a *marker*
  (`{"marker": True}`), usually meaning “play that section again”.
- `Capo`, `Key`/`Tom` and `Tuning` lines become metadata.
- Tablature and decoration lines (`e|--3--|`, `=====`) are dropped.

```pycon
>>> song = parse_chords_over_lyrics("Verse 1:\nC       G\nHello there my friend")
>>> song.text
'Hello there my friend'
>>> [(a.start, a.body["symbol"]) for a in song.of_kind("chord")]
[(0, 'C'), (8, 'G')]
>>> song.of_kind("section")[0].body["label"]
'Verse 1'
```

### Functions

| [`is_chord_line`](_autosummary/songleaf.parse.html.md#songleaf.parse.is_chord_line)(line)                            | True if every token is a chord or chord-line filler, and at least one is a chord.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`is_chord_token`](_autosummary/songleaf.parse.html.md#songleaf.parse.is_chord_token)(token)                          | True if `token` reads as a chord symbol (`G`, `F#m7b5`, `E7(#9)`, `C/G`).           |
| [`parse_chords_over_lyrics`](_autosummary/songleaf.parse.html.md#songleaf.parse.parse_chords_over_lyrics)(raw, \*[, meta, ...]) | Parse chords-over-lyrics text into a `Song`.                                        |

### songleaf.parse.is_chord_line(line)

True if every token is a chord or chord-line filler, and at least one is a chord.

```pycon
>>> is_chord_line("G   D/F#   Em  (x2)")
True
>>> is_chord_line("Bad Dad")
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### songleaf.parse.is_chord_token(token)

True if `token` reads as a chord symbol (`G`, `F#m7b5`, `E7(#9)`, `C/G`).

```pycon
>>> is_chord_token("Bb7(4)(9)"), is_chord_token("A7/sus4"), is_chord_token("Bridge")
(True, True, False)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### songleaf.parse.parse_chords_over_lyrics(raw, , meta=None, provenance=None)

Parse chords-over-lyrics text into a `Song`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **raw** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The chord chart, chord lines column-aligned over lyric lines.
  * **meta** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Metadata to start from (`title`, `artist`, …); `capo`,
    `key` and `tuning` found in the text are added to it.
  * **provenance** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Where the text came from, stored as is.
* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)


# _autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md

# songleaf.render

Render a song onto one dense page, with the lyrics as large as will fit.

A [`SheetLayout`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.SheetLayout) is one way of laying a song out: where the chords go
(`chords`), which lines share a row (`packing`), how many `columns`, and
whether sections, repeated lines and chord functions are `shading`-ed.
[`render_sheet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.render_sheet) draws any layout, and [`render_dense_a4()`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.render_dense_a4) is the v1
layout. A layout can be named by a spec that joins the options of
[`LAYOUT_OPTIONS`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.LAYOUT_OPTIONS) with `+` ([`layout_named()`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.layout_named)), and
[`make_renderer()`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.make_renderer) turns a spec into the `(song, output) -> dict` function
that the `renderer=` seam of [`songleaf.tools.sheet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.sheet) takes.

Every layout finds the largest lyric font size at which the whole song fits on
one page ([`fit_font_size()`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.fit_font_size)), then draws it:

- consecutive lines of a paragraph share a row, separated by a light `/`: as
  many as fit (`packing="greedy"`), or breaking where the lyrics break
  (`"structured"`: between couplets and quatrains, not inside a rhyming pair
  or a repeat; see [`songleaf.packing`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#module-songleaf.packing)). A blank line or a new section
  starts a new row, and a line too long for its column wraps at a space (inside
  a word only when a single word is wider than the column);
- `chords="over"`: chords ride on their lyric row, smaller and in a lighter
  colour, overlapping the letters instead of taking a line of their own. A chord
  starts over the syllable it lands on, and a `timing="before"` chord ends
  there. `DenseStyle.chord_rise` sets how deep they overlap: the tops of the
  letters by default, the words themselves with the `overlap` option;
- `chords="inline"`: chords sit in the lyric line itself, in a lighter colour,
  right before the syllable they land on. A chord that sounds before its
  syllable is preceded by a small marker (`DenseStyle.before_marker`);
- `columns=2`: the rows flow down two columns, under a full-width heading;
- `shading`: chorus-like sections get a light warm band and pre-chorus or
  bridge sections a light cool one, lines sung earlier in the song are set in
  dark grey, and chords are coloured by their function in the key estimated
  from the chords ([`songleaf.harmony`](_autosummary/songleaf.harmony.html.md#module-songleaf.harmony)): the tonic darker, the key’s other
  chords in the usual blue, chords outside the key in a warm accent;
- section labels are small grey prefixes (`V1`, `Ch`) on a section’s first row;
- only a song that cannot fit at `min_font_size` spills onto more pages.

Text is set in DejaVu Sans, a TrueType font bundled in `songleaf/data/fonts`
(Bitstream Vera licence, which allows embedding and redistribution; the licence
text is beside the files) and embedded in each PDF. It covers Latin Extended
(Turkish ş ğ ı), Greek, Cyrillic and more, where reportlab’s built-in Helvetica
stops at its single-byte cp1252 encoding (songleaf#9). If a bundled file cannot
be loaded, the matching Helvetica is used instead, with a warning. Emoji are
not covered by either.

```pycon
>>> short_label("Verse 1"), short_label("Pre-Chorus"), short_label("Coda")
('V1', 'Pre', 'Coda')
>>> layout = layout_named("inline+two-column")
>>> layout.chords, layout.columns, layout.packing
('inline', 2, 'greedy')
```

| [`PACKERS`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.PACKERS)          | The line packers a [`SheetLayout`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.SheetLayout) can name (see [`songleaf.packing`](_autosummary/songleaf.packing.html.md#module-songleaf.packing)). |

  * **columns** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Columns per page.
  * **shading** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Shade sections, repeated lines and chord functions.
  * **diagrams** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `"piano"` or `"guitar"` draws the song’s chords as a strip
    of diagrams at the foot of the first page ([`songleaf.diagrams`](_autosummary/songleaf.diagrams.html.md#module-songleaf.diagrams));
    the lyrics shrink to make room. `None`: no diagrams.
  * **score** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Draw the song’s score snippet, if its provider has one, above
    the line it belongs to ([`songleaf.snippets`](_autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md#module-songleaf.snippets)); the lyrics shrink
    to make room.
  * **style** ([`DenseStyle`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.DenseStyle)) – Typography and colours.

### songleaf.render.render_sheet(song, output, , layout='dense', page_size='A4', margin=14.0, min_font_size=6.0, max_font_size=72.0, scale=1.0, snippets=None)

Render `song` in `layout` (a [`SheetLayout`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.SheetLayout) or a spec) as a PDF to `output`.

The lyric font size is the largest that fits the song on one page, times
`scale`: `1` fills the page, `0.8` leaves room, `1.2` is larger type
that runs onto a second page. It never goes past `max_font_size`.

`snippets` provides a `score` layout’s snippet: `song -> ScoreSnippet | None`
(default [`songleaf.snippets.abc_snippet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md#songleaf.snippets.abc_snippet)).

`output` is a path or a binary file object. Returns
`{"path", "font_size", "pages", "rows"}`; `path` is `None` when
`output` is a file object.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# _autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md

# songleaf.snippets

Score snippets on the sheet (songleaf#12): which stretch of a song, and a small staff for it.

A snippet is a few bars of notation drawn above one line of the lyrics, for a
sense of the melody or the rhythm. Three parts, each replaceable:

- **Which stretch**: [`choose_segment()`](_autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md#songleaf.snippets.choose_segment) picks a line by rule (the first line
  of the chorus, else the most repeated line, else the first line), and
  [`mark_segment()`](_autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md#songleaf.snippets.mark_segment) records the choice, with the notation, as the song’s
  > `score` annotation ([`songleaf.model.score_link()`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.score_link)). A recorded annotation
  > wins over the rule, so it is how a choice is overridden.
- **What to draw**: a *snippet provider*, `song -> ScoreSnippet | None`, is
  injected into [`songleaf.render.render_sheet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#songleaf.render.render_sheet) (`snippets=`) and never
  imported by it. The default, [`abc_snippet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md#songleaf.snippets.abc_snippet), draws the short ABC notation
  recorded on the annotation with reportlab lines only: one voice, treble staff,
  notes, rests, accidentals, bar lines and chord names, placed as on a treble staff
  (no clef is drawn). Fuller engraving
  (MusicXML, whole ABC tunes) belongs in a provider behind an optional extra.
- **Where it goes**: the `score` layout option makes the renderer place the
  snippet as a row above its line; the font fit counts its height, so the
  lyrics shrink to make room.

ABC subset read by [`parse_abc()`](_autosummary/songleaf.snippets.html.md#songleaf.snippets.parse_abc): notes `A-G a-g` with `,` / `'`
octave marks, `^` `_` `=` accidentals, lengths `2` `/2` `3/2` `/`
(the unit is an eighth note), rests `z`, bar lines `|` `||` `|]` `|:`
`:|`, and `"G"` chord names over the next note. A length that needs a tie
(`5`) is refused. Header lines (`K:G`), decorations (`!fermata!`) and
anything else (ties, slurs, spaces) are skipped.

```pycon
>>> [(n.pitch, n.length) for n in parse_abc("C2 D/2 z |").notes]
[(28, 0.25), (29, 0.0625), (None, 0.125)]
```

# _autosummary/songleaf.songbook.html.md

# songleaf.songbook

A songbook: several songs in one PDF, with a table of contents, page numbers and bookmarks.

`render_songbook(songs, output)` renders each song through the same renderer
a single sheet uses (so each is at its fitted size), puts a table of contents
in front, stamps “page n of N” at the foot of every page and adds one PDF
bookmark per song. The renderer is a seam, as in [`songleaf.tools.sheet()`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.sheet).

### Functions

| [`render_songbook`](_autosummary/songleaf.songbook.html.md#songleaf.songbook.render_songbook)(songs, output, \*[, title, ...])   | Render `songs` (`(key, song)` pairs, in set-list order) as one PDF to `output`.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### songleaf.songbook.render_songbook(songs, output, , title='Songbook', renderer=None, page_size='A4', toc_size=12.0, footer_size=8.0)

Render `songs` (`(key, song)` pairs, in set-list order) as one PDF to `output`.

`output` is a path or a binary file object. `renderer` is a
`(song, output) -> dict` renderer (default: the dense layout). Returns
`{"path", "title", "pages", "songs": [{"key", "title", "artist", "page"}]}`
where `page` is the song’s first page in the book.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md

# songleaf.sources

Where songs are found: sources, and a search that composes them.

A *source* is any object with a `name`, a
`search(query, *, title, artist, lyrics, limit) -> list[Hit]` method and a
`get(song_id) -> Song` method that raises `KeyError` for an id it does not
have ([`get_song()`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.get_song) reports that as [`SongNotFound`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.SongNotFound); a source that cannot
load its data at all raises [`SourceUnavailable`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.SourceUnavailable)). [`search()`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.search) and [`get_song()`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.get_song) take
several through `sources=`; the default is the Kaggle chords-and-lyrics
corpus, read through `sung`.

A hit’s [`Hit.key`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.Hit.key) (`"<source>:<id>"`) names the song everywhere: it is
what [`get_song()`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.get_song) resolves and what the store is keyed by.

[`search_tiers()`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.search_tiers) is the one-field search: the songs whose title, artist or lyrics
match a query, each reported once, in the first of those that matches. A source may answer
it itself with a `search_tiers(query, *, limit)` method (the Kaggle sources do, in one
pass); any other source is asked three times through `search`.

### Module Attributes

| [`KAGGLE_CHORDS_ZIP`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.KAGGLE_CHORDS_ZIP)   | Where a copy of the corpus zip is found under the data root, before sung looks.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SONG_TIERS`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.SONG_TIERS)          | a song is in the first that fits.                                                 |

### Functions

| [`default_sources`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.default_sources)()                           | The sources used when none are given, built once per process.                                                                           |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`get_song`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.get_song)(key, \*[, sources])                | The song named by `key` (`"<source>:<id>"`), from the source of that name.                                                              |
| [`kaggle_chords_zip`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.kaggle_chords_zip)()                         | The corpus zip under the data root (`datasets/` + [`KAGGLE_CHORDS_ZIP`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.KAGGLE_CHORDS_ZIP)), if there is one. |
| [`search`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.search)([query, title, artist, lyrics, ...]) | Search every source and merge the hits, best first.                                                                                     |
| [`search_tiers`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.search_tiers)(query, \*[, limit, sources])   | Every source's songs whose title, artist or lyrics match `query`, by where they match.                                                  |

The Kaggle *chords-and-lyrics* corpus (~135K songs, chords over lyrics).

Read through `sung` from a local copy of the zip, with no Kaggle
credentials needed when that copy exists. The corpus was scraped from a
chords site: personal use only (licence tag `gray`).

Title and artist are matched fuzzily (typos, punctuation and word order
do not matter); lyrics must contain every word of the `lyrics` query as a
whole word. Lyrics matches are not ranked beyond popularity.

* **Parameters:**
  * **loader** – `() -> pandas.DataFrame` with `columns`. Defaults to
    sung’s loader of the local corpus zip.
  * **min_score** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Fuzzy-match cutoff, 0-100.

#### get(song_id)

The song with this id, parsed into a `Song`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)

#### search(query='', , title='', artist='', lyrics='', limit=10)

Songs matching every given constraint, best first.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Hit`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.Hit)]

#### search_tiers(query, , limit=10)

The songs whose title, artist or lyrics match `query`, by where they match.

`{"title": [...], "artist": [...], "lyrics": [...]}`, at most `limit` in each,
best first. A song is in the first kind it matches, even when it ranks below the
limit there, so a song is never shown as an artist match because more titles
matched.

Title and artist match word by word ([`WordIndex`](_autosummary/songleaf.match.html.md#songleaf.match.WordIndex)): the query
is inside the field (`"wonder"` finds *Wonderwall*) or the field is inside the
query (`"wonderwall oasis"` finds the title *Wonderwall* and the artist *Oasis*),
a word of four letters or more forgiving a typo; or every word of the query is in
the title or in the artist (`"paper boats invented band"`). A song whose title
holds a word of the query that its artist does not is a title match
(`"wonderwall oasis"`: *Wonderwall (ver. 2)* by Oasis), otherwise an artist match. Within each kind, the songs whose
title and artist together hold the most words of the query come first (so
*Wonderwall* by Oasis leads), then the closest by fuzzy score (of the title, or of
title and artist, whichever is closer; of the artist), then the most popular.
Lyrics hold every word of the query, rank by popularity, and carry
`meta["snippet"]`: the line that matched, with its spans.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Hit`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.Hit)]]

### *class* songleaf.sources.LocalFolderSource(root=None, , name='local_folder')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A folder of files you exported yourself, indexed and searched by name.

For files a chords/tab site lets a paying user export – Ultimate Guitar’s
Guitar Pro/PDF downloads, MuseScore’s MusicXML/MSCZ/MIDI/PDF exports – with
no automated route into either site (songleaf#5, songleaf#6): the user
exports the file through the site as usual and drops it here. No network
calls, no login; this only reads what is already on disk.

Text files (`.txt`, `.cho`, `.chopro`, `.crd`, `.pro`) are parsed
as chords-over-lyrics charts, the same format as the Kaggle corpus. Files
with no lyrics to parse (Guitar Pro, MusicXML, MSCZ, MIDI, PDF) become a
[`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song) with empty text and one
[`score_link()`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.score_link) annotation pointing at the file, so a
renderer can still show it as an attached score snippet.

A file is named `"Artist - Title.ext"` (the artist part is optional; a
plain `"Title.ext"` works too).

* **Parameters:**
  * **root** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Directory to index (searched recursively). Defaults to the
    `imports` data dir (`~/.local/share/songleaf/imports/`,
    moved by `SONGLEAF_DATA_DIR`).
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Registry name (default `"local_folder"`).

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, pathlib
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> _ = (pathlib.Path(root) / "Nobody - Paper Boats.txt").write_text(
...     "C\nla la la"
... )
>>> local = LocalFolderSource(root)
>>> hit = local.search("paper boats")[0]
>>> (hit.title, hit.artist)
('Paper Boats', 'Nobody')
>>> local.get(hit.id).of_kind("chord")[0].body["symbol"]
'C'
```

#### get(song_id)

The song at this relative path, parsed if it’s a chart, else score-linked.

* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)

#### search(query='', , title='', artist='', lyrics='', limit=10)

Substring-match the query/title/artist against each file’s name.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Hit`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.Hit)]

The corpus zip under the data root (`datasets/` + [`KAGGLE_CHORDS_ZIP`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.KAGGLE_CHORDS_ZIP)), if there is one.

`limit` in each; each song in the first kind it matches. Within a kind, each

# _autosummary/songleaf.store.html.md

# songleaf.store

Where songs persist: a `MutableMapping` of songs, JSON files by default.

Data lives under `~/.local/share/songleaf/<kind>/` (`songs/` for the store,
`sheets/` for rendered PDFs); `SONGLEAF_DATA_DIR` overrides the root.
Keys are song keys (`"<source>:<id>"`). Each song is one JSON file named after
its key, percent-encoded so that any key is a safe file name, and two keys that
differ only in letter case never share a file on a case-insensitive file system.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> from songleaf.model import Song
>>> songs = song_store(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> songs["demo:1"] = Song("la la la", meta={"title": "Demo"})
>>> list(songs), songs["demo:1"].title
(['demo:1'], 'Demo')
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DATA_DIR_ENVVAR`](_autosummary/songleaf.store.html.md#songleaf.store.DATA_DIR_ENVVAR)   | Environment variable overriding the data root.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`data_dir`](_autosummary/songleaf.store.html.md#songleaf.store.data_dir)(kind)        | The directory holding one kind of data (created if missing).      |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`file_name_of_key`](_autosummary/songleaf.store.html.md#songleaf.store.file_name_of_key)(key) | The file name a song key is stored under.                         |
| [`song_store`](_autosummary/songleaf.store.html.md#songleaf.store.song_store)([rootdir]) | Songs as JSON files in `rootdir` (default: the `songs` data dir). |

### songleaf.store.DATA_DIR_ENVVAR *= 'SONGLEAF_DATA_DIR'*

Environment variable overriding the data root.

### songleaf.store.data_dir(kind)

The directory holding one kind of data (created if missing).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### songleaf.store.file_name_of_key(key)

The file name a song key is stored under.

Every byte but lowercase ASCII letters, digits and `-_.` is percent-encoded
(uppercase letters included), so the name is safe everywhere and distinct from
every other key’s name even when letter case is ignored.

```pycon
>>> file_name_of_key("kaggle_chords:0"), file_name_of_key("src:Abc")
('kaggle_chords%3A0.json', 'src%3A%41bc.json')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### songleaf.store.song_store(rootdir=None)

Songs as JSON files in `rootdir` (default: the `songs` data dir).

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)]


# _autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md

# songleaf.timing

Play-along: a song’s media links and line timings (songleaf#30).

- **Media** ([`with_media()`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.with_media)): the song’s recording on YouTube or Spotify, as ids
  in `meta["media"]` (`{"youtube": "dQw4w9WgXcQ"}`), checked against each
  service’s id format so the page can embed a player without trusting free text.
- **Timings** ([`with_lrc()`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.with_lrc)): an `.lrc` file (or LRCLIB’s synced lyrics) gives
  a time per lyric line; [`align_lrc()`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.align_lrc) matches its lines to the song’s lines by
  word overlap (token F1, in order, skipping what does not match), and each matched
  line gets a `"time"` annotation: a point at the line’s start,
  `body={"ms": 61230, "source": "lrc"}`. \*\*Only the times are kept, never the
  LRC’s text\*\*, so a song’s lyrics stay the ones it was imported with.

The page then follows the recording: the line whose time has come scrolls into
view.

```pycon
>>> from songleaf.model import Song
>>> song = Song("Paper boats on a stream\ncarry the names of a dream")
>>> lrc = "[ar:Someone]\n[00:12.50]Paper boats on the stream\n[00:17.00]Carry the names of my dream"
>>> timed = with_lrc(song, lrc)
>>> [(a.start, a.body["ms"]) for a in timed.of_kind("time")]
[(0, 12500), (24, 17000)]
```

### Module Attributes

| [`GetJson`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.GetJson)   | how [`fetch_lrclib()`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.fetch_lrclib) reaches the network (inject it).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`fetch_lrclib`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.fetch_lrclib)(title, artist, \*[, duration_s, ...]) | LRCLIB's synced lyrics (LRC text) for a song, or None.                             |
| [`parse_lrc`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.parse_lrc)(text)                                    | `(milliseconds, line text)` per timed line of an LRC, sorted by time.              |
| [`token_f1`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.token_f1)(a, b)                                     | Word-overlap F1 of two lines (case and punctuation ignored).                       |
| [`with_lrc`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.with_lrc)(song, lrc_text, \*[, source])             | `song` with `"time"` annotations from an LRC (earlier ones replaced).              |
| [`with_media`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.with_media)(song, \*\*ids)                          | `song` with media ids set in `meta["media"]` (an empty id removes one).            |

how [`fetch_lrclib()`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.fetch_lrclib) reaches the network (inject it).

* **Type:**
  `(url, params) -> JSON`

alias of [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]], [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)]

### songleaf.timing.align_lrc(song, lrc, , min_f1=0.5, lookahead=4)

`(line start offset, ms)` pairs: LRC lines matched in order to the song’s lines.

Each LRC line is matched to the best of the next `lookahead` unmatched song
lines with lyrics, if its token F1 is at least `min_f1`; an LRC line that
matches none is skipped (an ad lib, a line the song does not have).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

### songleaf.timing.fetch_lrclib(title, artist, , duration_s=None, get_json=None)

LRCLIB’s synced lyrics (LRC text) for a song, or None. Use it with
[`with_lrc()`](_autosummary/songleaf.timing.html.md#songleaf.timing.with_lrc), which keeps the times only.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### songleaf.timing.parse_lrc(text)

`(milliseconds, line text)` per timed line of an LRC, sorted by time.

A line with several time tags (a repeated chorus) appears once per tag; an
`[offset:+/-ms]` tag shifts every time (positive: earlier, as the format says);
metadata tags (`[ar:...]`) and untimed lines are skipped.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### songleaf.timing.token_f1(a, b)

Word-overlap F1 of two lines (case and punctuation ignored).

```pycon
>>> token_f1("Carry the names", "carry the NAMES of my dream")
0.6667
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### songleaf.timing.with_lrc(song, lrc_text, , source='lrc', \*\*align_kwargs)

`song` with `"time"` annotations from an LRC (earlier ones replaced).

Only the times are added; the LRC’s text is used to align and then dropped.

* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)

### songleaf.timing.with_media(song, \*\*ids)

`song` with media ids set in `meta["media"]` (an empty id removes one).

```pycon
>>> from songleaf.model import Song
>>> with_media(Song("la"), youtube="dQw4w9WgXcQ").meta["media"]
{'youtube': 'dQw4w9WgXcQ'}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song)


# _autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md

# songleaf.tools

The single source of truth for every surface: plain functions, flat arguments, JSON-ready results.

The CLI (`python -m songleaf`) is `cw` over [`TOOLS`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.TOOLS). Nothing here
knows about any surface. `sources`, `store` and `renderer` are the seams:
library callers pass them, the CLI hides them. Code that wants objects rather
than dicts uses [`songleaf.sources`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#module-songleaf.sources), [`songleaf.store`](_autosummary/songleaf.store.html.md#module-songleaf.store) and
[`songleaf.render`](_autosummary/songleaf.render.html.md#module-songleaf.render) directly.

### Module Attributes

| [`TOOLS`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.TOOLS)   | Every operation, in the order the CLI lists them.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`export`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.export)(query, \*[, format, transpose, ...])       | Export a song as ChordPro (`chordpro`) or plain text with chords over lyrics (`text`).                     |
| [`forget`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.forget)(key, \*[, store, library_root])            | Remove a song from the stored songs, from every list it was in, and from every Viewed list.                |
| [`import_file`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.import_file)([path, title, artist, url, ...])      | Read pasted song text from a file (`-`: standard input) and store it; see `import_text`.                   |
| [`import_text`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.import_text)(text, \*[, title, artist, url, ...])  | Store a song pasted from anywhere: Ultimate Guitar markup, ChordPro, OpenSong or plain chords over lyrics. |

Every operation, in the order the CLI lists them.

### songleaf.tools.build_index(, path='')

Build the search index of the Kaggle corpus, once, where the corpus zip is.

Searching then reads the index instead of loading the whole corpus into
memory (tens of MB instead of over a GB per process). Run it again after
replacing the zip. `path` defaults to beside the zip under the data root.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.export(query, , format='chordpro', transpose=0, output='', pick=1, refresh=False, sources=None, store=None)

Export a song as ChordPro (`chordpro`) or plain text with chords over lyrics (`text`).

`query` is a song key or a search, as for `sheet`. `transpose` moves every chord
by that many semitones (the stored song keeps its chords). The result has the `text`;
with `output` set it is also written to that file, and `path` says where.
ChordPro is the fleet’s interchange (Songbook Pro, OnSong and the ChordPro app read it);
chords that sound before their syllable travel in the `x_songleaf_before` directive.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.forget(key, , store=None, library_root=None)

Remove a song from the stored songs, from every list it was in, and from every Viewed list.

It can be found and stored again by searching. Returns `{"key", "deleted"}`;
`deleted` is False when it was not stored.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.import_file(path='-', , title='', artist='', url='', format='', store=None)

Read pasted song text from a file (`-`: standard input) and store it; see `import_text`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.import_text(text, , title='', artist='', url='', key='', capo='', format='', store=None)

Store a song pasted from anywhere: Ultimate Guitar markup, ChordPro, OpenSong or plain chords over lyrics.

The format is detected (`format` forces one of `ultimate-guitar`,
`chordpro`, `opensong`, `chords-over-lyrics`). `url` is only
recorded as provenance: songleaf never contacts it (an official or Pro
Ultimate Guitar URL is refused). The song is stored under `paste:<hash>`
(the same text, the same key), or `ug:<id>` for an Ultimate Guitar URL,
and is then usable like any other: `sheet <key>`, `song <key>`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.import_url(url, , refresh=False, store=None, source=None)

Fetch one community Ultimate Guitar chord page and store its chart as `ug:<id>`.

Local command line only, and off unless `SONGLEAF_UG_URL=1` is set: prefer
pasting, or the bookmarklet run on the page you opened (see
`songleaf.ultimate_guitar`). Official and Pro pages are refused. A chart
already stored is not fetched again unless `refresh`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.media(query, , youtube='', spotify='', pick=1, store=None, sources=None)

Link the song’s recording: a YouTube video id and/or a Spotify track id.

An id given as `""` is left as it is; `"-"` removes it. Returns
`{"key", "media"}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.search(query='', , title='', artist='', lyrics='', limit=10, list_songs=3, sources=None, store=None, library_root=None)

Find songs with one query: in your lists’ names, then titles, artists and lyrics.

With only `query`, every song comes once, tagged with where it matched (`match`):
`"list"` (the first `list_songs` stored songs of each list whose name the query
names; `list` and `list_name` say which, and the list’s other songs are found in
the later kinds as usual), then `"title"`, `"artist"` and `"lyrics"`, in that order,
at most `limit` of each, best first within each. A song that matches its title and
its lyrics is a title match only. `highlight` holds the matched words of the title and
artist (and of `list_name`) as `[start, end]` spans; a lyrics match carries
`snippet`, the line that matched, with its spans.

With `title`, `artist` or `lyrics`, it is a narrower search instead: songs that
match every field given (and `query`, fuzzily over title and artist), `match: ""`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### songleaf.tools.sheet(query, , output='', pick=1, refresh=False, layout='dense', transpose=0, scale=1.0, sources=None, store=None, renderer=None)

Make a one-page song sheet (PDF) for the best match of `query`.

`query` may also be a song key, as `search` and `songs` show them
(`kaggle_chords:1234`): a stored song renders without searching, and the
key of a known source is fetched from it directly. `pick` chooses the n-th
best match instead of the best. The song is saved to the store; `refresh`
fetches it from its source again, replacing the stored copy. The PDF goes to
`output`, by default the `sheets` data directory.

`layout` is `dense` (the default), or options joined with `+`:
`overlap` (chords over the words themselves), `inline` (chords in the
line, before their syllable), `packed` (rows break where the lyrics do),
`two-column`, `shaded` (sections, repeated lines and chord functions);
for example `inline+packed+two-column`. A `renderer` decides the layout
itself, so it does not go with `layout` or `scale`.

`transpose` moves every chord by that many semitones (spelled for the new
key); the stored song keeps its chords. `scale` multiplies the font size
that fills the page: `0.8` for smaller type, `1.2` for larger type over
more pages.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.snippet(query, notation, , line=0, pick=1, store=None, sources=None)

Put a score snippet over one line of a song; the `score` layout draws it on the sheet.

`notation` is a few bars of ABC (`"G2 AB c2 | d4"`; the unit is an eighth
note). `line` is the 1-based lyric line it goes with; `0` lets the rule
choose (the first line of the chorus, else the most repeated line, else the
first). Returns `{"key", "start", "end", "rule"}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.song(query, , pick=1, refresh=False, transpositions=6, sources=None, store=None)

The song itself as JSON: lyrics text, chords and sections, and every key it can move to.

`query` is a song key or a search, as for `sheet`; the song is stored
the same way. Besides the song’s own fields (`text`, `annotations`,
`meta`, `provenance`), the result has `chords` (the distinct chords,
in order of first appearance), `sections` (`{"start", "end", "label",
"family"}`, the family as the printed sheet shades it: `"chorus"`,
`"bridge"` or `""`), `song_key` (the estimated key, `""` with
no chords) and `transpositions`: one table per shift from
`-transpositions + 1` to `transpositions` semitones, each
`{"semitones", "key", "chords": {original: transposed}}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.songbook(group, , output='', title='', layout='dense', scale=1.0, library_root=None, sources=None, store=None, renderer=None)

Render a list (group) of songs as one PDF: a table of contents, then every song at its fitted size.

`group` is a list’s id or its name (the best match of the name). The
songs come in the order they were filed in the list, nested lists
included, so the list order is the set list. Page numbers are stamped on
every page and each song is a PDF bookmark. `title` defaults to the
list’s name. `layout` and `scale` are as for `sheet`. The PDF goes to
`output`, by default the `sheets` data directory.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.songs(, store=None)

The keys of the stored songs.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### songleaf.tools.sync(query, , lrc='', lrclib=False, pick=1, store=None, sources=None, get_json=None)

Time the song’s lines from an LRC, so the page can scroll with the recording.

`lrc` is the LRC text (an `.lrc` file’s content); with `lrclib` and no
`lrc`, LRCLIB is asked for the song’s synced lyrics. Only the times are stored
(`"time"` annotations), never the LRC’s text. Returns `{"key", "timed",
"lines"}`: how many lyric lines got a time, of how many.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.unview(key, , user='', library_root=None)

Take a song out of `user`’s Viewed list. It stays stored, and in its lists.

Returns `{"key", "removed", "viewed_at"}`: when it had been viewed, so the same
time can be given back to [`view()`](_autosummary/songleaf.tools.html.md#songleaf.tools.view) to undo.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.view(key, , user='', at=0.0, store=None, library_root=None)

Put a stored song at the top of `user`’s Viewed list: they just opened it.

`at` (seconds since the epoch) records that time instead, which is how an undo puts
a song it took out back where it was. Returns `{"key", "viewed_at"}`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### songleaf.tools.viewed(, user='', store=None, library_root=None)

The songs `user` opened, the most recent first: `key`, `title`, `artist`, `viewed_at`.

`user` is who the host says is asking (no one: the list everyone shares). Songs no
longer stored are left out. `viewed_at` is in seconds since the epoch.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]


# _autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md

# songleaf.ultimate_guitar

Ultimate Guitar: community chord charts the reader opened themselves (songleaf#28).

A community “Chords” or “Tabs” page on ultimate-guitar.com carries its chart in
the page’s store (`.js-store`’s `data-content`, or `window.UGAPP.store`):
`page.data.tab_view.wiki_tab.content`, in `[ch]`/`[tab]` markup, with the
tab’s `song_name`, `artist_name`, `tonality_name` and the view’s `capo`.

“Official” and “Pro” pages are refused: their content lives in UG’s own player,
behind its subscription, and songleaf does not circumvent content protection
(terms of service, section 6.2). [`refusal()`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.refusal) says why, in words a reader
understands; the bookmarklet (`data/web/bookmarklet.js`) applies the same rule
in the browser, and [`songleaf.importers.import_song()`](_autosummary/songleaf.importers.html.md#songleaf.importers.import_song) applies it to every
import that names a UG URL.

Three routes, in the order songleaf prefers them (the terms are in
`misc/docs/sources.md`):

1. paste the chart into the page (no contact with UG at all);
2. the bookmarklet, run in the reader’s own browser on a page they opened: it
   reads the chart from that page and hands it to songleaf’s import form, where
   the reader confirms it;
3. [`UltimateGuitarURLSource`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.UltimateGuitarURLSource), which fetches one URL per call. It is for a
   local command line only: off unless `SONGLEAF_UG_URL=1` is set, never in
   [`songleaf.sources.default_sources()`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.default_sources), never behind an HTTP route, and it
   > never searches.

All UG-derived songs carry `provenance.license = "personal"`.

```pycon
>>> refusal("https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/invented/song-official-123")[:22]
'This is an official or'
>>> refusal("https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/invented/song-chords-123")
''
>>> ug_key("https://tabs.ultimate-guitar.com/tab/invented/song-chords-123")
'ug:123'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`URL_SOURCE_ENVVAR`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.URL_SOURCE_ENVVAR)     | The environment variable that turns on [`UltimateGuitarURLSource`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.UltimateGuitarURLSource) (`"1"`).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`REFUSED_TYPES`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.REFUSED_TYPES)         | Tab types whose page has no text chart songleaf may read (UG's own player, or video).                                      |
| [`USER_AGENT`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.USER_AGENT)            | What a request for a page says it is (UG scores bots; songleaf does not pretend to be a browser).                          |
| [`FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) | Seconds before a page fetch gives up.                                                                                      |
| [`MAX_PAGE_BYTES`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.MAX_PAGE_BYTES)        | Bytes read from a page at most (a chart page is a few hundred KB).                                                         |

### *class* songleaf.ultimate_guitar.UltimateGuitarURLSource(\*, fetch=<function fetch_page>, enabled=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One UG chord page, by URL: local command line only, off by default.

It never searches ([`search()`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.UltimateGuitarURLSource.search) returns nothing) and is never among
[`songleaf.sources.default_sources()`](_autosummary/songleaf.sources.html.md#songleaf.sources.default_sources). [`get()`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.UltimateGuitarURLSource.get) fetches the one page
it is given, refuses official and Pro pages, and returns the chart as a
[`Song`](_autosummary/songleaf.model.html.md#songleaf.model.Song) keyed `ug:<id>` (see [`ug_key()`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.ug_key)).

* **Parameters:**
  * **fetch** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – `url -> html`; the default makes one plain HTTPS request.
  * **enabled** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Whether fetching is allowed; defaults to `SONGLEAF_UG_URL=1`.

#### get(url)

The chart at *url* as a song (raises [`RefusedPage`](_autosummary/songleaf.ultimate_guitar.html.md#songleaf.ultimate_guitar.RefusedPage), or `ValueError` when off).

#### search(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Nothing: this source reads the one page it is given and never searches UG.

  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

# _autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md

# songleaf.viewed

Each viewer’s *Viewed* list: the songs they opened, the most recent first.

Kept on the server, one JSON document per viewer under the data root
(`library/viewed/<viewer>.json`: `{"views": {song key: seconds since the epoch}}`).
A viewer is whoever the host says is asking (the platform’s user id, under enlace); the
file is named after a hash of that id ([`viewer_file_stem()`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.viewer_file_stem)), so no identity is
written to disk in the clear. With no identity (a local run, or a host with no login),
everyone shares one list, `anyone`.

Viewed is not a list of the library: it is never in `groups.json`, a song leaves it
without leaving any list, and leaving it does not delete the song.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> _ = record_view("x:1", root=root, at=100.0)
>>> _ = record_view("x:2", root=root, at=200.0)
>>> [v["key"] for v in read_viewed(root=root)]
['x:2', 'x:1']
>>> remove_view("x:2", root=root)
200.0
>>> [v["key"] for v in read_viewed(root=root)], read_viewed(user="someone", root=root)
(['x:1'], [])
```

### Module Attributes

| [`ANYONE`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.ANYONE)    | The file stem of the list everyone shares when the host names no viewer.         |
|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`MAX_VIEWS`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.MAX_VIEWS) | The most songs one Viewed list keeps; opening one more forgets the least recent. |

### Functions

| [`drop_everywhere`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.drop_everywhere)(key, \*[, root])       | Take `key` out of every viewer's list (the song was deleted); returns how many held it.         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`read_viewed`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.read_viewed)(\*[, user, root])          | `user`'s Viewed list, the most recent first: `[{"key", "viewed_at"}]`.                          |
| [`record_view`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.record_view)(key, \*[, user, at, root]) | Put `key` at the top of `user`'s Viewed list (or at time `at`); returns the time used.          |
| [`remove_view`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.remove_view)(key, \*[, user, root])     | Take `key` out of `user`'s Viewed list; returns when it was viewed, `None` if it was not there. |
| [`viewer_file_stem`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.viewer_file_stem)(user)                 | The file name (without `.json`) of `user`'s list: a hash of the id, never the id.               |

### songleaf.viewed.ANYONE *= 'anyone'*

The file stem of the list everyone shares when the host names no viewer.

### songleaf.viewed.MAX_VIEWS *= 2000*

The most songs one Viewed list keeps; opening one more forgets the least recent.

### songleaf.viewed.drop_everywhere(key, , root=None)

Take `key` out of every viewer’s list (the song was deleted); returns how many held it.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> _ = record_view("x:1", root=root); _ = record_view("x:1", user="b", root=root)
>>> drop_everywhere("x:1", root=root), read_viewed(user="b", root=root)
(2, [])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

### songleaf.viewed.read_viewed(, user=None, root=None)

`user`’s Viewed list, the most recent first: `[{"key", "viewed_at"}]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### songleaf.viewed.record_view(key, , user=None, at=None, root=None)

Put `key` at the top of `user`’s Viewed list (or at time `at`); returns the time used.

`at` puts a song back where it was (an undo of [`remove_view()`](_autosummary/songleaf.viewed.html.md#songleaf.viewed.remove_view)).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### songleaf.viewed.remove_view(key, , user=None, root=None)

Take `key` out of `user`’s Viewed list; returns when it was viewed, `None` if it was not there.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### songleaf.viewed.viewer_file_stem(user)

The file name (without `.json`) of `user`’s list: a hash of the id, never the id.

```pycon
>>> viewer_file_stem(None), viewer_file_stem("")
('anyone', 'anyone')
>>> stem = viewer_file_stem("user-1234")
>>> stem.startswith("u-") and len(stem) == 34 and "1234" not in stem
True
>>> stem == viewer_file_stem("user-1234") != viewer_file_stem("other")
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# For AI agents

`songleaf` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/songleaf/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/songleaf/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`songleaf.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/songleaf/songleaf.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/songleaf/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
